details:
I would like to suggest separating World Moderation and Group Moderation into two clearly defined systems.

World creators should continue to have the moderation tools that VRChat considers appropriate for managing their worlds. However, when a Group instance is created, moderation authority should come from the group hosting that instance rather than automatically being shared with the world's creator.

For Group instances, VRChat could provide a dedicated Group Instance Moderation API that works specifically with the group hosting the instance.

The API should only allow moderation actions when all of the following are true:

The instance is owned or hosted by the group.

The person performing the action has the required moderation permission within that group.

The moderation action applies only within the appropriate group or group instance.

Authorized group staff could then use moderation actions such as:

Warn

Kick

Force Mute

Ban

These functions should not be available to ordinary group members simply because they are members of the group. They should require explicit staff/moderation permissions assigned by the group.

For example:

Public world instance:

 World moderation rules and permissions apply.

Group instance:

 The hosting group's moderation permissions apply.

Group staff member with moderation permission:

 Can use the Group Instance Moderation API.

Regular group member:

 Cannot call moderation functions.

I think separating these systems would make it much clearer who actually has authority inside an instance.

It would also make API permissions safer because third-party moderation tools would not simply receive unrestricted moderation abilities. Any moderation request would still have to be validated against the staff member's actual group permissions.

Moderation actions performed through the Group Moderation API should also be recorded in the group's Audit Log so owners and administrators can see who performed an action and who it was performed against.

VRChat has already added group-instance kick and warn information to Group Audit Logs, including who initiated the action and whom the action affected. Expanding that model to a dedicated group moderation system could make moderation easier to understand and audit.

The purpose of this suggestion is not to give groups unlimited moderation power. It is to establish a clear boundary:

World moderation manages the world. Group moderation manages the group's instances.

This would allow group staff to build and use moderation tools for their own communities without giving those tools authority outside of the group's own instances.
title: Separate World Moderation and Group Moderation Permissions
